codificacao-posicional.d: Any mechanism that tells attention where each token is in the sequence: absolute embeddings (APE), relative biases or rotations (RoPE). Without one, attention is blind to order.

equivariancia-permutacao.d: A property of attention without position: shuffling the input tokens just shuffles the outputs the same way, \( \operatorname{Attn}(PX) = P\,\operatorname{Attn}(X) \). To it, a sentence is a “bag of tokens”.

ape.d: Absolute Position Embedding: adds a vector \( p_m \), sinusoidal or learned in a table, to the embedding of token \( m \). A learned table has a fixed size and doesn't exist past its last row. GLM-5.3 uses a minimal 4-position APE inside the indexer pool.

posicao-relativa.d: A family of encodings that adds to the attention score a bias that depends only on the distance \( i-j \) (T5's buckets, ALiBi's penalty).

rope.d: Rotates each pair of dimensions of q and k by an angle \( m\,\theta_i \) proportional to the position. Since \( R_m^\top R_n = R_{n-m} \), the score ends up depending only on the distance between the tokens. It is applied before the key is written to the KV cache.

rope-theta.d: The base \( b \) of the RoPE frequencies, \( \theta_i = b^{-2i/d_r} \). Larger bases stretch the wavelengths of the slow pairs. In the recipes: 10⁴ (DeepSeek's SWA and the drafters), 1.6·10⁵ (DeepSeek's compress_rope_theta) and 10⁷ (Qwen).

comprimento-de-onda.d: How many tokens a RoPE pair takes to make one full turn: \( \lambda_i = 2\pi/\theta_i \). Pairs with \( \lambda_i \) larger than the training context never completed a turn, and they are the ones that extrapolate.

cos-sin-cache.d: A precomputed table with \( \cos m\theta_i \) and \( \sin m\theta_i \) for each position \( m \). The kernel reads the row for the position and applies \( \tilde q = q\odot\cos + \operatorname{rot}(q)\odot\sin \), without building the rotation matrix.

rope-parcial.d: Applying RoPE to only part of the dimensions of each head and leaving the rest without position (NoPE). Qwen3.8 rotates 64 of 256 dims; DeepSeek-V4 rotates the last 64 of 512.

partial-rotary-factor.d: The config field that sets the fraction of the head that gets RoPE: \( d_r = \rho\cdot d_{\text{head}} \). In Qwen3.8 it is 0.25 (64 of 256 dims).

neox-style.d: vLLM's RoPE pair convention. True (NeoX, rotate_half): pair \( i = (i, i + d_r/2) \). False (interleaved, GPT-J): pair \( i = (2i, 2i+1) \). Using the wrong convention scrambles the position without raising any error. DeepSeek-V4 uses False.

nope.d: Attention with no explicit positional encoding at all. Order arrives through the causal mask and through other layers, such as recurrences and convolutions. GLM-5.3's MLA layers are NoPE (qk_rope_head_dim = 0).

mrope.d: RoPE with position in three coordinates \( (t, h, w) \), time, height and width, with the frequency pairs split among them (mrope_section). For text, \( t=h=w \) and it becomes plain RoPE. Qwen3.8 uses [11, 11, 10], interleaved.

extrapolacao-de-posicao.d: Serving positions beyond the training context without adjusting RoPE. The slow pairs produce never-seen angles, and the attention scores fall outside the learned distribution.

interpolacao-de-posicao.d: Extending the context by dividing every position (or frequency) by a factor \( s \). It keeps the angles within the known range, but reduces the resolution between neighbors in the fast pairs.

ntk-aware.d: Extends the context by changing the RoPE base, \( b' = b\cdot s^{d_r/(d_r-2)} \): the fastest pair stays intact and the slowest is divided by exactly \( s \).

yarn.d: A context extension method that treats each RoPE pair according to the number of turns it made during training: fast pairs intact, slow ones interpolated by factor and a ramp in between (β_fast/β_slow), plus a temperature correction (mscale). Qwen ×4 (optional); DeepSeek ×16, only on the compressor layers.

mscale.d: The factor \( 0.1\ln s + 1 \), an empirical fit from the YaRN paper, which multiplies cos/sin and therefore the logits by its square: it sharpens the softmax to compensate for the more “spread-out” attention in long contexts. For \( s=4 \), mscale ≈ 1.139 and logits × 1.296; for \( s=16 \), ≈ 1.277 and × 1.63. DeepSeek-V4 doesn't use it: vLLM zeroes mscale and mscale_all_dim.

original-max-position-embeddings.d: The reference training context \( L \) that YaRN uses to classify the pairs and compute the target \( s\cdot L \). DeepSeek: 65,536 (×16 → 1,048,576). Qwen: 262,144 (×4 → ~1M).

max-position-embeddings.d: The config.json field that says how far the model was designed or trained to go. It is the basis from which vLLM derives the context cap. Qwen 262,144; DeepSeek and GLM 1,048,576.

max-model-len.d: The vLLM argument (--max-model-len) that sets the cap on tokens per request (prompt + output). It is a cap, not a KV reservation, but it sizes per-step buffers (indexer workspace, page tables).

allow-long-max-model-len.d: An environment variable that allows a max_model_len above the cap derived from the config (vLLM warns that it should be used “with extreme caution”). It only unlocks the check: what makes the positions valid is the RoPE scaling (YaRN).

rope-inverso.d: In DeepSeek-V4, K and V are the same vector, and V carries the rotation of each key's position. The attention output is rotated by position \( -i \) in the 64 RoPE dims so that the contribution becomes relative, before the output projection.

estado-compartilhado-mutavel.d: When several parts of the code write to the same object (here, the config.rope_parameters dictionary shared by all layers). The result ends up depending on the construction order. The vllm#54815 fix switched to a per-layer copy.
